chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'It is not allowed to you to take women afterwards, nor that you should change them for other wives, though their beauty be pleasing to you, except what your right hand possesses.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'I see that you are alleging that it is permissible for you whatever was not permissible for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and indeed Allah, the Exalted, permitted His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) to marry from the women whatever he wished.'
He only said 'It is not allowed to you to take women afterwards' after what He prohibited to you, as in His Words: 'Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters' up to the end of the verse.'

key_terms.لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ: It is not permissible for you

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'It is not allowed to you to take women afterwards' in Surah Al-Ahzab according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the restriction in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:52) applies specifically to the Prophet after the general prohibitions (like mothers and daughters) were established, confirming his unique privilege to marry more than the four wives limited to others. This interpretation underscores the concept of *khāṣṣiyyah* (special status) of the Prophet, distinguishing his marital permissions from those of the general community. The hadith highlights that while the Prophet had exclusive rights, these were not extended to the Ummah, reinforcing the distinct legal standing of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Prophet.
